# Test BlockForest 

```{r}
library(blockForest)
```

```{r}
# NOTE: There is no association between covariates and response for the
# simulated data below.
# Moreover, the input parameters of blockfor() are highly unrealistic
# (e.g., nsets = 10 is specified much too small).
# The purpose of the shown examples is merely to illustrate the
# application of predict.blockForest().


# Generate data:
################

set.seed(1234)

# Covariate matrix:
X <- cbind(matrix(nrow=40, ncol=5, data=rnorm(40*5)), 
           matrix(nrow=40, ncol=30, data=rnorm(40*30, mean=1, sd=2)),
           matrix(nrow=40, ncol=100, data=rnorm(40*100, mean=2, sd=3)))
colnames(X) <- paste("X", 1:ncol(X), sep="")

# Block variable (list):
block <- rep(1:3, times=c(5, 30, 100))
block <- lapply(1:3, function(x) which(block==x))

# Binary outcome:
ybin <- factor(sample(c(0,1), size=40, replace=TRUE), levels=c(0,1))

# Survival outcome:
ysurv <- cbind(rnorm(40), sample(c(0,1), size=40, replace=TRUE))



# Divide in training and test data:

Xtrain <- X[1:30,]
Xtest <- X[31:40,]

ybintrain <- ybin[1:30]
ybintest <- ybin[31:40]

ysurvtrain <- ysurv[1:30,]
ysurvtest <- ysurv[31:40,]




# Binary outcome: Apply algorithm to training data and obtain predictions
# for the test data:
#########################################################################

# Apply a variant to the training data:

blockforobj <- blockfor(Xtrain, ybintrain, num.trees = 100, replace = TRUE, block=block,
                        nsets = 10, num.trees.pre = 50, splitrule="extratrees", 
                        block.method = "BlockForest")


# Obtain prediction for the test data:

(predres <- predict(blockforobj$forest, data = Xtest, block.method = "SplitWeights"))
predres$predictions



# Survival outcome: Apply algorithm to training data and obtain predictions
# for the test data:
###########################################################################

# Apply a variant to the training data:

blockforobj <- blockfor(Xtrain, ysurvtrain, num.trees = 100, replace = TRUE, blocks=block,
                        nsets = 100, num.trees.pre = 50, splitrule="extratrees", 
                        block.method = "BlockForest")

blockforobj$paramvalues
blockforobj$biased_oob_error_donotuse

blockforobj$forest$forest
  
  
# Obtain prediction for the test data:

(predres <- predict(blockforobj$forest, data = Xtest))

predres <- predict(blockforobj$forest, data = Xtest, type = "se", se.method = "jack")

predres$chf
predres$survival
predres$unique.death.times

rowSums(predres$chf)
```


```{r}
library(survival)
concordance_index <- concordance(Surv(ysurvtest[,1], ysurvtest[,2]) ~ rowSums(predres$chf))
concordance_index

coef(concordance_index)
concordance_index$concordance
concordance_index$var
```

```{r}
library(survival)
# Create risk groups based on cumulative hazard estimates
risk_group <- ifelse(rowSums(predres$chf) > median(rowSums(predres$chf)), "high", "low")

surv_test <- survdiff(Surv(ysurvtest[,1], ysurvtest[,2]) ~ risk_group)
surv_test
```


```{r}
library(survival)
# Evaluate Brier score at each unique death time
times <- predres$unique.death.times

# Assuming the `pec` package is available
library(pec)
library(survival)
# Prepare data
y_surv <- Surv(ysurvtest[,1], ysurvtest[,2])


ibs_score <- pec::ibs(pec(object = list(blockForest = blockforobj), 
                          formula = y_surv ~ ., 
                          data = data.frame(Xtest), 
                          times = times))

```

```{r}
# Train the blockForest model with importance measure
blockforobj <- blockfor(Xtrain, ysurvtrain, num.trees = 100, replace = TRUE, blocks = block,
                        nsets = 100, num.trees.pre = 50, splitrule = "extratrees", 
                        block.method = "BlockForest", importance = "permutation")

variable_importance <- blockforobj$forest$variable.importance

# Calculate block-wise aggregated importance
aggregate_importance <- sapply(block, function(indices) {
  mean(variable_importance[indices])  # Mean importance of variables in each block
})
names(aggregate_importance) <- paste("Block", 1:length(block), sep="_")
aggregate_importance




blockforobj$forest$
# Retrieve block-wise importance
block_importance <- blockforobj$forest$importance.mode. 


block.importance
block_importance
```
